The 130EQ is seems to be a popular beginner scope, a lot of people have voiced their distaste for the red dot finderscope. I've always had trouble with it, spending ludicrous amounts of time finding objects in the eyepiece. Before the 130EQ I had a Celestron TravelScope70, that knackered when it fell into the ocean so the finderscope has been salvaged.

For anyone else with a 130EQ wanting to try this, the finderscope from the Travelscope70 fits perfectly, and it is ~27mm∅. A replacement finderscope should fit into the stock red dot tube so long as it just less than 27mm wide since the securing screws give a few mm tolerance. The very same replacement finderscope I used can be bought with obviously the Travelscope70 for £40, a Celestron starter accessory pack for £15, and I've seen some floating around on their own for ~£5. I would absolutely recommend doing this if you find one for £5.
The 130eq was my first scope as well. It's red dot finder was garbage and I replaced it with a Rigel reflex finder right away. Using the stock finder as a scope ring is a pretty cool idea
